# Benedict W. H. Dixon

> Personal site of Benedict W. H. Dixon. Building, leading & learning. Engineer turned operator: JPMorgan, American Express, a hedge fund, fintech, then co-founding companies. Co-founder, COO and CTO at kash. Three of us built kash's whole product. Mine was the fat middle, from the hooks the frontend calls down to indexing on-chain events.

Key facts:
- Started out as an engineer, building payment systems at JPMorgan, then on the R&D team for American Express's referral campaigns. After that came a hedge fund, fintech, and founding his own startups.
- Made a very conscious and intentional move from writing code to running companies and teams. When AI tooling arrived, went back to building.
- A strategic, product and technology advisor to early-stage startups and founders. Always interested to compare notes with people doing the work.

## Key pages

- [Home / About](https://benedictdixon.com/): About, career, writing, contact.
- [How I work with AI](https://benedictdixon.com/ai/): The standing map of the AI practice — the work, the tooling, the personal stack, the view.

- [For podcast hosts](https://benedictdixon.com/hosts/): Bio, photo, topics and past talks.

## The essays

<!-- build:essays -->
- [Why my AI spend has levelled off and my output is still rising](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/why-my-ai-spend-has-levelled-off/): Why a flat line in AI spend doesn’t mean AI has stopped paying, and why per-person budgets planned to rise with output are planning for hours nobody has.
- [The agent can’t be its own checker](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/the-agent-cant-be-its-own-checker/): Why an AI agent’s ‘done’ can’t close its own work in a company that moves real money, and what does instead.
- [AI collapsed the build, not the operation](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/ai-collapsed-the-build/): One person with AI can build what fifty used to. But the operation — incidents, maintenance, 3am — doesn’t collapse with the build. Why fewer people is the wrong read.
- [The unit of production has changed](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/the-unit-of-production-has-changed/): Three of us built kash; mine is the fat middle. AI didn’t just make the typing faster; it deleted the coordination overhead. The cap that’s left is judgement.
- [The assistant that knows you](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/the-assistant-that-knows-you/): Point your personal AI at your own second brain and it stops guessing: it answers from your notes, in your own words.
- [The assistant that’s always on](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/always-on-assistant/): A personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine, reaches you on the app you already text in, and only touches what you let it.
- [Building a Second Brain That Doesn’t Die](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/building-a-second-brain/): An opinionated second brain template for Obsidian PKM, wired for Claude Code — the three calls that make it stick when most systems die in three months.
- [In Clawd We Trust: A Year of Claude Code, Distilled](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/in-clawd-we-trust/): A practical Claude Code guide on how to use it effectively: the mental model, environment setup, phased workflow and quality practices that compound.
- [Tesserakt Protocol: Purpose-Built Infrastructure for AI Agents](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/tesserakt-protocol/): A purpose-built AI agent protocol for discovery, matching, negotiation and transaction at machine speed — six layered protocols for trustless commerce.
- [The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agents](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/the-missing-infrastructure-for-ai-agents/): AI agent infrastructure is missing: agents are forced through rails built for humans when they need machine-speed protocols and cryptographic identity.
- [Autonomous AI Agents: A Platform for Trustless Business Interactions](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/autonomous-ai-agents/): Autonomous AI agents can represent individuals and businesses on a trustless agent platform, executing decisions in milliseconds rather than weeks.
- [The Democratic Myth of DAOs: The road to autocracy](https://benedictdixon.com/writing/the-democratic-myth-of-daos/): DAO governance problems explained: how token-weighted voting slides toward oligarchy and autocracy under the banner of radical decentralisation.
<!-- /build:essays -->
